summary: Iteration 161 (Device-role registry + USB pairing UI + POS auto-print device routing) — full E2E verification on the live preview. Lint gate green (ruff + eslint + check-empty-states). Admin UI tested with Chromium (Web Serial + HID + USB all supported): all 8 roles render with correct testids; 13/13 transport-matched Pair buttons present (receipt_printer:serial+usb, label_printer:usb+serial, barcode_scanner:hid, nfc_reader:hid+usb, signature_pad:hid+usb, cash_drawer:serial, customer_display:serial+usb, scale:serial); all 8 roles initially show the 'Not paired' badge; injecting a fake pairing into localStorage ('5812:device-role-pairings') + clicking Refresh correctly flips receipt_printer to 'Paired (unplugged)' (paired=true, available=false because fingerprint doesn't match any real port) while leaving the other 7 roles untouched; Unpair button appears for the paired role only; clicking 'Pair Serial' DOES invoke navigator.serial.requestPort (verified by monkey-patching the API and observing the call). Pre-existing admin cards all still render (branding-editor-card, backup-restore-card, integrations-card, kiosk-links-card, security-checkpoints-card, module-access-manager-card). No backend tests run — backend was untouched this iteration per the brief. POS auto-print fallback verified by code inspection (ProductsPage.jsx:546-557): dynamic import of utils/printers, falls back to window.print() when device returns {printed:false} or the import throws. printers.js correctly returns {printed:false, fallback:true} when getDeviceForRole('receipt_printer') is null.

issues: Cancel-detection regex /cancel|no device/i in DevicePairingDialog.jsx:65 does not match Chrome's Serial-picker cancel message ('No port selected by user') nor the DOMException name 'NotFoundError'. Result: when a user cancels the Serial picker, they see a red error toast with the raw DOMException message instead of the friendly 'Pairing cancelled' info toast. HID picker cancel works correctly because Chrome's message contains 'No device selected'. Cosmetic only — suggested fix: change regex to /cancel|no (device|port)|notfound/i or test against e.name === 'NotFoundError'.

action_items: MINOR/COSMETIC: Broaden DevicePairingDialog cancel-message regex to also catch Chrome's Serial cancel ('No port selected by user') and the DOMException name 'NotFoundError' so user-cancels of all three pickers show 'Pairing cancelled' (info) instead of a red error toast.

MINOR/DOC: The PR brief lists testid 'module-access-card' as a pre-existing admin card but the actual rendered testid is 'module-access-manager-card' (in AdminPage.jsx:426). Not introduced this iteration — flag to keep PR descriptions in sync with code.
critical_code_review_comments: deviceRoles.js: storage helpers _read/_write swallow exceptions silently — safe (quota / disabled localStorage degrades to empty map). Fingerprinting strategy (vendor:product:serial) is the right cross-reload identity for USB and HID; for Serial, vendor+product alone is correct because Web Serial ports don't expose serial numbers.
pairDeviceForRole throws on user-cancel — caller (DevicePairingDialog.pair) catches and toasts. Public API is clean.

printers.js: printReceiptText tolerates already-open ports via the InvalidStateError catch — robust. ZPL/USB path correctly claims/releases interface. Both helpers return {printed:false, fallback:true} on error so the POS can fall back to window.print() — solid design.

ProductsPage.jsx:547-557 auto-print block uses dynamic import('../utils/printers') so the device-roles bundle isn't pulled into the main POS chunk if the store has auto_print_receipt disabled — good code-splitting.
DevicePairingDialog transportSupported() correctly returns false outside a browser and gates the amber 'no transports' banner — matches the spec.
No backend changes — diff confined to 3 frontend files + 1 admin import — appropriate scope.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (7/7 admin cards, 8/8 roles, 13/13 pair buttons, paired-state simulation, picker invocation, unpair UI — all pass)

seed_data_creation: Test injected one fake receipt_printer pairing into localStorage during the UI test (key='5812:device-role-pairings'). Only persists in the test browser context — no server-side data created.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Web Serial / HID / USB pairing requires a user-gesture browser picker that Playwright cannot drive end-to-end. The verification strategy that worked here: (a) monkey-patch navigator.serial.requestPort to record invocation + reject with NotFoundError, (b) seed localStorage directly with a fake pairing record (transport='serial', fingerprint='serial:VID:PID') and click the Refresh button to observe the dialog flip the role to 'Paired (unplugged)'. The 'unplugged' state is correct here because getDeviceForRole() looks up navigator.serial.getPorts() and finds no matching fingerprint. To exercise the 'Available' (green) badge you'd need real hardware OR a deeper patch that fakes navigator.serial.getPorts() to return a port whose getInfo() matches the seeded vendor/product IDs.
rca of the issue: N/A — no issues found beyond the cosmetic cancel-toast regex flagged above.
